literal: Saying 'we will extinguish fire with ghee' is like saying 'we will extinguish love by public rumor'.
translation: To think that one can extinguish love through public gossip is like trying to put out a fire by pouring ghee on it.
modern: நெய்யை ஊற்றி நெருப்பை அணைப்போம் என்று கூறுவது போலாகும், ஊரார் பேசும் வதந்தியைக் கொண்டு காதலை அடக்குவோம் என்று நினைப்பது.
explanation: This couplet uses a vivid analogy to show how public gossip (கௌவை) only intensifies secret love (காமம்) instead of suppressing it. Ghee is highly inflammable, and pouring it on a fire (எரி) will only make the flames leap higher, not extinguish (நுதுப்பேம்) them. Similarly, when the townspeople gossip about the lovers, their talk acts as fuel, heightening the lovers' desire and making their bond even stronger. The poet highlights the futility of trying to control or end a deep passion through social pressure and rumors.
